nodes.rationale: After order creation the system shows No order, Total tagihan, Rekening bank and Batas waktu pembayaran so the customer can transfer the exact amount to the correct account before the deadline; these same values are what admin later checks (cek nominal, cek rekening tujuan).

nodes.norm_label: status: ditolak + alasan penolakan (rejected with reason)
nodes.rationale: Rejection carries an explicit reason (alasan penolakan) so the customer knows what was wrong and can re-upload a corrected payment proof instead of the order being silently dropped.

nodes.label: Status: Menunggu konfirmasi (Awaiting confirmation)
nodes.source_location: page 1, annotation on Upload bukti pembayaran

nodes.label: Verifikasi pembayaran (Admin payment verification)
nodes.rationale: Verification is a manual four-point check (bukti transfer, nominal, rekening tujuan, mutasi rekening) because payment is a manual bank transfer with no automated gateway callback; the admin is the source of truth for whether money actually arrived.

nodes.label: Manual bank transfer payment with proof upload and admin verification
nodes.norm_label: manual bank transfer payment with proof upload and admin verification
nodes.rationale: The e-commerce flow deliberately uses manual bank transfer (customer transfers to a displayed bank account, uploads proof, admin verifies) instead of an automated payment gateway. Trade-off: no gateway integration or fees and simpler implementation, but it requires a 'Menunggu konfirmasi' intermediate state, manual admin work per order, a payment deadline (batas waktu pembayaran), a rejection path with a stated reason, and a customer re-upload loop for invalid proofs.

nodes.label: Order status lifecycle: Menunggu pembayaran -> Menunggu konfirmasi -> Dibayar | Ditolak -> Dikirim -> Selesai
nodes.norm_label: order status lifecycle: menunggu pembayaran -> menunggu konfirmasi -> dibayar | ditolak -> dikirim -> selesai
nodes.rationale: Each status marks a handoff between customer and admin: Menunggu pembayaran (waiting on customer transfer), Menunggu konfirmasi (waiting on admin verification), Dibayar/Ditolak (admin decision, Ditolak includes a reason so customer can re-upload), Dikirim (admin shipped), Selesai (customer confirmed receipt). This lets both roles see who owns the next action on an order.
nodes.source_location: page 1, status annotations across both flows

nodes.label: Admin Payment List Table
nodes.rationale: Plain data table with six header columns (No, Invoice, Customer, Metode, Status, Tanggal) and four sample rows: INV001/Andi/QRIS/Paid/10-07-2026, INV002/Budi/VA BCA/Pending/10-07-2026, INV003/Citra/E-Wallet/Expired/09-07-2026, INV004/Dedi/Transfer/Failed/09-07-2026. Status values are rendered in bold to draw the admin eye to payment outcome. AMBIGUOUS: the header row appears shifted one column left relative to the data (the 'No' column holds invoice IDs and the 'Tanggal' column is empty), which looks like a layout mistake in the mockup rather than intended design; an implementer should treat the six headers as the intended fields and expect a sequential 'No' index in front of the invoice ID.

nodes.label: Admin Role
nodes.rationale: The mockup is explicitly scoped to the Admin actor ('Admin dapat melihat informasi seperti'), implying payment management is a back-office (admin dashboard) feature rather than a customer-facing page.

nodes.label: Invoice Number Field (INV001..INV004)
nodes.rationale: Invoice identifiers follow the pattern 'INV' + zero-padded sequence (INV001), suggesting a human-readable invoice code separate from a database primary key.

nodes.label: Payment Method Field (Metode)
nodes.rationale: Four sample channels are shown (QRIS, VA BCA, E-Wallet, Transfer), which are the standard Indonesian online payment options; this implies the checkout supports multiple payment channels, most likely via a payment gateway.

nodes.label: Payment Status Field
nodes.rationale: Rendered in bold in the mockup so the outcome of each payment is the most scannable element in the row.

nodes.label: Transaction Date Field (Tanggal)
nodes.rationale: Dates are displayed in DD/MM/YYYY format (10/07/2026), the Indonesian convention.

nodes.label: VA BCA (Virtual Account BCA) Payment Method
nodes.norm_label: va bca (virtual account bca) payment method

nodes.label: Payment Management Module (Admin Reference Mockup)
nodes.rationale: Reference mockup titled 'Pada Modul Manajemen Pembayaran' describing what an Admin can see in the payment management module of the PT IKN e-commerce site. Design intent: give admins a single tabular overview of every invoice, its customer, payment channel, payment outcome and date so they can reconcile and follow up on orders.

nodes.label: Payment Status Lifecycle (Pending -> Paid / Expired / Failed)
nodes.norm_label: payment status lifecycle (pending -> paid / expired / failed)
nodes.rationale: The four statuses form a typical payment-gateway lifecycle: a new payment starts Pending, becomes Paid on successful settlement, Expired when the customer does not pay before the deadline, or Failed when the gateway rejects the transaction. Having distinct Expired and Failed states (rather than one generic 'unpaid') lets admins distinguish customers who never paid from technical/declined payments, which matters for follow-up. The status set mirrors gateway conventions (e.g. Midtrans settlement/pending/expire/failure), so the module likely mirrors webhook statuses from a payment provider - INFERRED.

nodes.label: PT Industri Karet Nusantara (Nusantara Rubber Industry)
nodes.norm_label: pt industri karet nusantara (nusantara rubber industry)

nodes.label: Desaturated Cool-Tinted Photo Treatment
nodes.rationale: The photo is heavily desaturated with a pale cyan/teal sky and a near-monochrome white building, dark glass, and grey asphalt. Inferred trade-off: a muted, low-contrast palette keeps the hero background from competing with overlaid text and brand accent colours, at the cost of a less vivid, somewhat flat look.

nodes.label: Head Office Photo as Website Hero
nodes.norm_label: head office photo as website hero
nodes.rationale: A wide, low-angle exterior shot of the corporate head office with the company name legible on the facade is used as the home page hero of the ikn-fe Next.js site. Design intent (inferred from the public/img/home.png path): establish credibility and physical presence of PT Industri Karet Nusantara as an established rubber manufacturer, rather than leading with product imagery. The building is framed off-centre with a large empty sky area, leaving room for overlaid headline text.

nodes.label: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
nodes.description: Blue hard hats with a gear emblem, white surgical-style face masks and white cotton gloves worn by the workers.
nodes.rationale: Showing full PPE in production imagery signals workplace safety compliance (K3) and professionalism to website visitors and B2B buyers.

nodes.label: Slab Cutter Machine
nodes.description: Blue-painted industrial cutter with a large circular steel blade, roller feed bed and motor-driven shaft, used to chop coagulated rubber slabs into smaller pieces.

nodes.label: Produksi Karet 1 (ikn-fe public image)
nodes.description: Byte-identical copy of Images/produksi-karet-1.webp deployed as a static asset under ikn-fe/public/img so the Next.js site can serve it at /img/produksi-karet-1.webp. Depicts workers cutting coagulated rubber on a slab cutter with drying racks of crumb rubber behind.

nodes.label: Production Showcase Photography
nodes.description: Design intent behind the produksi-karet image series: real-people, real-machinery photography used on the company website to illustrate the production/process section.
nodes.rationale: Authentic factory photos build credibility for a B2B rubber company; the -1 suffix indicates this is the first of a numbered series intended for a gallery, carousel or process-steps section on the Next.js site.

nodes.label: Rubber Slab Cutting Stage
nodes.description: Early mechanical stage of crumb rubber processing in which coagulated slabs are size-reduced before washing, creping and drying.
nodes.rationale: Cutting the raw slab into smaller pieces exposes contaminants for washing and makes downstream milling/creping feasible; it is the first value-adding step the factory performs on farmer-supplied rubber.

nodes.label: Crumb Rubber (SIR) Production Process
nodes.description: End-to-end processing of field-coagulated natural rubber into Standard Indonesian Rubber (SIR) crumb: slab cutting, washing, creping, drying on racks, then baling.
nodes.rationale: The website production photos are meant to document this process visually so that buyers understand IKN processes raw karet into standardized export-grade product rather than merely trading it.

nodes.label: Rubber Processing Factory Floor
nodes.description: Indoor industrial setting with concrete walls, heavy machinery and racks; the physical environment of the natural rubber processing plant.

nodes.label: Coagulated Natural Rubber (Raw Material)
nodes.description: Large brown lump of field-coagulated latex (cup lump / slab, bahan olah karet) being fed into the cutter; the raw input of crumb rubber processing.

nodes.label: Crumb Rubber Drying Racks
nodes.description: Multi-tier steel trolley rack stacked with sheets/blankets of processed crumb rubber wrapped in plastic, with a green marker tag and batch number 005/202 written on the frame.

nodes.label: Branded Worker Uniform
nodes.description: Navy polo shirts carrying a multicolor wave logo on the chest and a triangular mountain-style emblem on the shoulder; the wave logo resembles a plantation-company (Perkebunan Nusantara style) mark, so the photo may originate from a partner/parent estate rather than PT IKN itself. Reading of the logo text is uncertain.

nodes.label: Produksi Karet 1 (Images source asset)
nodes.description: Photo (1920x1080 webp) of two rubber factory workers in blue hard hats, face masks, gloves and navy branded polo shirts feeding a large lump of coagulated natural rubber into a slab cutter machine with a circular steel blade; behind them a steel trolley rack holds stacked, plastic-wrapped crumb rubber blankets tagged 005/202. Source copy kept in the top-level Images folder.

nodes.label: Rubber Factory Workers
nodes.description: Two male production operators handling raw rubber by hand on the factory floor; the human element of the production photo.

nodes.label: Rubber Tapping Photo (ikn-fe/public/img/karet-1-1-scaled.jpg)
nodes.description: Byte-identical copy of Images/karet-1-1-scaled.jpg placed in the Next.js public/img directory so it can be served as a static asset on the PT IKN website.

nodes.label: Rubber Tapping Photo (Images/karet-1-1-scaled.jpg)
nodes.description: Landscape photo (2560x1440) of a tapped rubber tree: fresh white latex runs down a diagonal tapping cut, along a small metal spout, and drips into a dark, weathered collection cup wired to the trunk. Blurred green plantation in the background. The -scaled suffix indicates a WordPress-style resized export of a larger original.

nodes.label: Raw Material Origin Imagery
nodes.rationale: Design intent (inferred): a wide 16:9 stock-style photo of latex tapping is suited for a hero banner or about/company-profile section on a rubber company website. It signals provenance and authenticity of the rubber products sold on the e-commerce site. The shallow depth of field and empty left half give room for overlaid headline text.

nodes.label: Rubber Tapping (Penyadapan Karet)
nodes.rationale: The photo captures the moment of tapping itself (latex actively flowing) rather than a finished product, communicating that PT IKN's rubber originates from real plantation harvesting. This is the core process the company's supply chain starts from.

nodes.label: E-commerce Product Catalog Image Asset
nodes.rationale: Static asset under Next.js public/img, served as a product listing image for the PT IKN storefront; isolated on a white background with a wide 16:9 framing suited to product cards and hero/gallery slots.

nodes.label: Rubber Retaining Loop Tab
nodes.rationale: Small molded rubber loop on the face of the sheath, likely used to strap or tie the sheath onto the blade or to hang the covered tool.

nodes.label: Sarung Egrek (Rubber Egrek Blade Sheath)
nodes.rationale: Flat, fan/trapezoid-shaped black rubber sheath with a curved outer edge and an open slot along one side into which the curved egrek blade slides. Photographed on a white background as an isolated e-commerce product shot.

nodes.label: Blade Protection and Worker Safety
nodes.rationale: A sheath for an egrek exists to cover the sharp curved blade during transport and storage, preventing injury to plantation workers and protecting the blade edge from damage. Rubber is chosen because it is flexible, durable, weather-resistant, and cheap to mold, which fits a rubber manufacturer product line.

nodes.label: Amber Granular Resin Flakes
nodes.rationale: Physical form shown in the image: irregular, translucent, reddish-orange to amber chips/granules of roughly 3-10 mm, with some darker fragments and fine orange dust. This is the sellable form of the product.

nodes.label: Natural Rubber (Karet Alam)
nodes.rationale: Raw material feedstock from which cyclized rubber resin is derived; ties the product to IKN's core business as a rubber company.

nodes.label: Paint, Ink and Adhesive Binder
nodes.rationale: Typical end use of cyclized rubber resin: a binder/film-former in paints, printing inks, adhesives and coatings. Not visible in the image; inferred from the product class.

nodes.label: Resiprene 35
nodes.rationale: Product name taken from the file name. Resiprene 35 is a cyclized natural rubber resin product associated with PT Industri Karet Nusantara (IKN); the photo is consistent with that identity (amber, glassy, brittle resin chips).

nodes.label: Zip-Lock Sample Bag
nodes.rationale: A clear resealable plastic bag with a red-striped seal is shown open and partially filled with the granules. Design intent: signal that the product is supplied as loose bulk granules and that small sample quantities are available to buyers.

nodes.label: Resiprene 35 Product Photo
nodes.rationale: Close-up product photograph on a white background: a large heap of translucent amber-orange resin granules with a clear zip-lock sample bag spilling the same granules in the foreground. Shot to show material color, translucency and granular form for the product listing on the IKN e-commerce site.

nodes.label: Cyclized Rubber Resin
nodes.rationale: Material class: natural rubber chemically cyclized into a hard, thermoplastic, solvent-soluble resin. The glassy amber appearance in the photo is characteristic of this material class.

nodes.label: Plantation and Industrial Workwear Use
nodes.description: Intended use as protective footwear for wet, muddy plantation fields (rubber, oil palm) and industrial or agricultural sites, implied by the tall shaft, lug sole, and PTPN branding.

nodes.label: Rubber Safety Boots (Sepatu Boots Karet)
nodes.description: Knee-high, pull-on, black rubber boots with reinforced toe and heel and an aggressive anti-slip lug sole; a finished rubber product sold by PT IKN.

nodes.label: E-commerce Product Catalog Image
nodes.description: Pattern of serving static product photos from the Next.js public/img directory for use on product listing and detail pages.
nodes.rationale: Static assets in public/ are served directly by Next.js without a build step, so product photos can be swapped by the client without touching code; a consistent white-background style keeps the catalog grid visually uniform.

nodes.label: Perkebunan Nusantara (PTPN) Co-branding
nodes.description: Perkebunan Nusantara wordmark with a green/yellow/blue curved-stripe emblem on the right boot shaft, indicating the product belongs to the Perkebunan Nusantara (PTPN) plantation holding group of which PT Industri Karet Nusantara is a subsidiary.

nodes.label: Sepatu Boots Product Photo
nodes.description: Product photo of a pair of tall black rubber boots on a plain white background, shot at a three-quarter angle. The shaft carries the IKN triangle logo on the left boot and a Perkebunan Nusantara wordmark with a green/yellow/blue stripe emblem on the right boot. Reinforced toe cap, heel counter, and deep-lug tread sole are visible.
nodes.rationale: Isolated white-background studio shot with no props is the standard e-commerce catalog style: it lets the image sit cleanly on product cards and detail pages of the Next.js storefront and keeps the brand marks on the shaft legible.

nodes.label: IKN Logo Branding
nodes.description: Red/green triangular mark with the letters IKN beneath it, moulded or printed on the upper shaft of the left boot.

nodes.label: Natural Rubber (Karet) Material
nodes.description: Vulcanised natural rubber compound giving the boots a waterproof, flexible, glossy black finish; the core material PT IKN processes.

nodes.label: Blue Triangle Emblem
nodes.rationale: Equilateral blue triangle with a smaller white triangular cutout in its centre (hollow delta) and a subtle bevelled edge. It functions as the icon mark of the brand and can stand alone as a favicon or app icon. The delta/triangle shape suggests stability, strength and growth, a common choice for industrial brands.

nodes.label: Boxed RUBIN Wordmark
nodes.rationale: The word RUBIN in a wide geometric sans-serif, all caps, blue on white, enclosed in a thin blue rectangular border whose width matches the triangle base. The box anchors the emblem and makes the lockup read as a single unit.

nodes.label: Brand Blue Color
nodes.rationale: Single-color identity: one medium cyan-blue (approximately #0A7BC2) is used for the emblem, the wordmark and the border; white is the only other colour. This makes the logo reproducible in one ink and suitable as the primary accent colour for the website theme.

nodes.label: PT IKN
nodes.rationale: The Indonesian rubber company that owns this website project. The logo image does not mention IKN, so the link between the RUBIN brand and PT IKN is inferred only from the repository context.

nodes.label: RUBIN Brand
nodes.rationale: The brand name carried by the logo is RUBIN, not IKN. It is most likely the trade/product brand under which PT IKN markets its rubber products, but the image itself gives no textual link to PT IKN.

nodes.label: Transparent-Background Logo Asset
nodes.rationale: The filename suffix removebg-preview indicates the background was stripped with a remove.bg-style tool and exported at preview (low) resolution. The result is a PNG with alpha channel intended for UI overlay; the preview resolution may limit use at large sizes.

nodes.label: RUBIN Logo (transparent PNG)
nodes.rationale: Stacked logo lockup: a solid blue triangle emblem sits above a rectangular box containing the wordmark RUBIN. Background is transparent so the mark can be overlaid on the website header, navbar, footer and print material.

nodes.label: RUBIN Logo Image
nodes.description: Logo asset: a solid blue equilateral triangle with a white hollow triangular center (beveled/3D edge), above a white rectangular box outlined in blue containing the uppercase wordmark RUBIN in blue. Stored in the Next.js public image folder of the PT IKN frontend.

nodes.label: Blue Brand Color
nodes.rationale: The logo uses a single medium/corporate blue against white for both the triangle and the wordmark, giving a monochrome, trustworthy, industrial visual identity that is easy to reproduce on web and print.

nodes.label: Blue Triangle Mark
nodes.rationale: Primary pictorial mark of the RUBIN logo: a hollow blue triangle (delta shape) with a subtle 3D bevel. A triangle conventionally signals stability, strength and upward growth, fitting an industrial/material brand; the hollow center keeps the mark light and reproducible at small sizes.

nodes.label: RUBIN Brand
nodes.rationale: RUBIN is the brand name presented by this logo. Given the asset lives in the PT IKN (Indonesian rubber company) frontend, RUBIN is likely a rubber product brand, partner, or sub-brand shown on the e-commerce site; the exact relationship to PT IKN is not stated in the image itself.

nodes.label: RUBIN Wordmark
nodes.rationale: Uppercase sans-serif text RUBIN enclosed in a thin blue-outlined rectangle beneath the triangle, functioning as a name plate that anchors the pictorial mark and makes the brand name legible on its own.
